claim: Rank correlation (correlating two orderings by applying the product-moment correlation to ranks) is Spearman's method, from this source.
quote:
Precis ely  the  same
 method  of  calculation  may  be  again  used  in  the  latter  case,
 simply  substituting  the  inverse  ranks,  97,  8o,  etc .,  for  the  per-
 formances,  8,000,  6,000,  etc.
locator: Part I Sec. 3 'Comparison by Rank', p. 80 (printed; PDF p. 10)
issue: The source substitutes ranks into the product-moment formula, which is the statistic now called Spearman's rho. Note the source's product-moment formula takes deviations from medians, not means (p. 77); for untied ranks the two coincide.

claim: The source defines the statistic named rho.
quote:
The relation  is as follows:
 R=I--  3Sd
 n -  I
 where  Sd is the sum  of the differences  of rank  for all the indi -
 viduals,
locator: Part I Sec. 4(d) 'Method of rank differences', p. 87 (printed; PDF p. 17)
issue: The symbol rho and the closed form 1 - 6 sum d^2 / n(n^2 - 1) do not appear in this paper: it writes the product-moment coefficient as r and its own rank-difference coefficient as R, a different statistic (the footrule). A reader who opens the source for 'rho' finds R. Citing Spearman 1904 for rho is the field's convention, so this is a naming gap, not a misattribution.

claim: Rank correlation measures how closely two series order the same items.
quote:
It depends  upon  noting  how  much  each  individual's  rank  in
 the one faculty  differs  from  his rank  in the other  one;  evidently,  
 this  will be nil when  the correlation  is perfect,  and will increase
 as the correlation  diminishes.
locator: Part I Sec. 4(d), p. 86 (printed; PDF p. 16)
issue: Supports the reading of a rank correlation as agreement of two orderings; the application to attackers ordering MTDs by NCR reduction is ours.

claim: Caption names rho as Spearman's rank correlation (uncited; the name is covered by U0609's citation).
quote:
Precis ely  the  same
 method  of  calculation  may  be  again  used  in  the  latter  case,
 simply  substituting  the  inverse  ranks,  97,  8o,  etc .,  for  the  per-
 formances,  8,000,  6,000,  etc.
locator: Part I Sec. 3, p. 80 (printed; PDF p. 10)
issue: Naming is a true negative, covered by U0609. The caption's 95 % intervals for rho are not from this source (it gives only a probable error under no correlation, for R); they rest on U0605's 'otherwise a percentile bootstrap', so check there that rho is meant to fall under 'otherwise'.
